meta.notes: Firmware 1.4.15 and later: user presets hold 32 bands (fosi-audio-ds3-8-band covers older firmware). Limits are those of Fosi's web control center: freq 20 to 20000 Hz, Q 0.1 to 20, gain ±30 dB, pre-gain -24 to 0 dB in whole dB (checked in the app on 1.4.6) (the pre-gain command itself takes -50 to 0). Presets as read on 1.4.6 and 1.6.10: the 7 built-in ones (0 to 6) hold 8 bands on every firmware and are named by the device ("CLASIC" sic; the web app shows Classic); the user presets are 7 to 9. The web app offers the DAC filter and upsampling in UAC 2.0 mode, upsampling from firmware 1.4.9, and game mode in UAC 1.0 mode; it turns upsampling off before turning the EQ on, and the reverse. Switching the UAC mode, or game mode to FPS or 7.1, reconnects the device. The EQ still applies in FPS and 7.1 game modes (heard on 1.6.10). In UAC 2.0 mode the DS3 is 0x152a:0x889b, which the ZH3 shares; in UAC 1.0 mode it is 0x20b1:0x80d5 (XMOS's vendor id, read on firmware 1.4.6). Reported quirk, not corrected (D39): devicePEQ reports that filters come out wider than the Q sent as gain grows (Q / 10^(|gain|/40)), and that shelf frequencies move with gain.

meta.notes:
devicePEQ lists its product id in its SchemeNo16 group (walkplay-schemeno16-devices), which no longer matches it. Its official presets: 1 Default (flat), 2 Rock, 3 Vocal, 4 Instrumental, and the game presets 5 FPS Footsteps, 6 FPS Gunshots, 7 Vocal Boost, 8 Immersion Mode, 10 bands each, pre-gain 0. The app shows the channel balance as one slider from -50 to 50 and writes it as a cut of one channel (n > 0 cuts the left by n dB, n < 0 the right); the device holds a gain per channel, which are the two controls here. Warnings, seen on firmware 0.3: the first report after the device has been idle for some minutes is lost (a band write the app sent first after about 6 minutes didn't take; sent again, it did); a quick run of mic gain writes left it at -4.5 dB, which no write asked for; after the app's pre-gain writes the pre-gain read (0x03) answered +1 dB, though it reads back the handler's writes. setEnabled(false) doesn't turn its EQ off (see the base). It also takes shelves, which the app doesn't offer. The device fills only the bytes it answers with and leaves the rest of its report as the last one left it, so the app shows a cut-short firmware version ("0.") and a wrong balance after some reads; the handler reads past that.
Microphone gain: NICEHCK's app offers whole dB, but the device rounds what it's sent to the nearest 1.5 dB and reads that back (every half dB from -12 to +12 written and read back on 2026-10-31), so the control's step is 1.5. The app follows a mic gain write with [1,0x04], and the device ignores a request sent within about 50 ms of it. Switching the work mode, the device ignores requests for up to about 250 ms (measured 2026-10-31); the DAC filter, gain level and volume answer at once.

meta.notes:
Seeded from AutoEQ by scripts/import/seed.ts. Band count, gain range and peaking Q range from AutoEQ's PEQ_CONFIGS QUDELIX_5K, which is an optimizer setting: the engine may allow more bands. The frequency range and the shelves' Q range are assumptions. USB identity from a devicePEQ recorded capture. Steps are the USB write's resolution (freq 1 Hz, gain 0.1 dB, Q 1/1024), with Q's minimum moved onto that grid (corrected 2026-10-02). The second USB identity (0x4007, "Qudelix-5K USB DAC") is a maintainer's unit, added 2026-10-03; devicePEQ's capture has 0x4005 "... 48KHz". 0x0a12 is the Bluetooth chip vendor's id, shared with other devices (FiiO's among them), so the vendor alone says nothing.
Protocol: the USB protocol is write-only. devicePEQ dropped the device for that; the bridge keeps it, marked experimental.

From the User's Guide ADI-2 DAC v1.8, §12.2 Subpage Parametric EQ: band 1 is Peak, Shelf, High Cut or High Pass; bands 2-4 are fixed to Peak; band 5 is Peak, Shelf or High Cut. Gain -12 to +12 dB in 0.5 dB steps. Frequency 20 Hz (200 Hz for bands 4 and 5) to 20 kHz, 'in steps between 1 Hz and 100 Hz': the guide doesn't say where the step changes, so the frequency domains are left continuous and the device rounds. Q 0.5 to 9.9 on bands 1-3 and 0.5 to 5.0 on bands 4-5, in steps of 0.1. Cut and pass filters are 12 dB/oct, at the band's Q. The guide calls the shelf of bands 1 and 5 just 'Shelf' and doesn't say which way it faces: a low shelf on band 1 and a high shelf on band 5 is an assumption to confirm on the device. There is no EQ preamp: the DSP has 24 dB of internal headroom (§13) and Volume must be lowered for large boosts. With Dual EQ on, left and right have their own settings, which v1 profiles don't describe; this profile is the linked (default) setting. Bass/Treble is a separate engine: rme-adi-2-dac-fs-bass-treble. The USB product name carries the unit's serial number ('ADI-2 DAC (51120366)'), so the match uses ids only; they come from a Linux hardware report, not from RME. Draft until checked: written from the manual alone and not yet tried on a device or reviewed. Open points: which way the band 1 and band 5 shelves face, the frequency grid, whether the original ADI-2 DAC (the alias) has the same EQ and USB ids.

From the User's Guide ADI-2 DAC v1.8, §12.3 Subpage Bass / Treble: a bass shelf at 20-150 Hz in 1 Hz steps (default 85 Hz, Q 0.9) and a treble shelf at 3-10 kHz in 100 Hz steps (default 6.5 kHz, Q 0.7), each -6 to +6 dB in 0.5 dB steps, Q 0.5 to 1.5. The guide gives no Q step, so Q is left continuous. This engine runs alongside the 5-band PEQ (rme-adi-2-dac-fs). Loudness (§12.4) adds to it and is not described here. The match is shared with the PEQ profile, told apart by engine; see its notes for where the USB ids come from. Draft until checked: written from the manual alone and not yet tried on a device or reviewed. Open points: the Q step, whether the original ADI-2 DAC (the alias) has the same EQ and USB ids.
